script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, October 26. Here is the week's news.

Independent School District 622's board met Monday night on a 2026 referendum update and a revision of the 2026-2027 school calendar for ACT testing.

Superintendent Tucci Osorio gave the referendum update. The agenda also listed an acknowledgment of contributions, a consent agenda with disbursements and change orders, and actions to set the time and agenda for the November 9 work study session and to set a special meeting to canvass the election.

The agenda prints no dollar amounts for the referendum update or the consent items.

The meeting was at six in the evening. Speakers fill out a public comment sign-up sheet, state their name, and receive between two and four minutes. Public comment lasts no longer than thirty minutes.

Student school board representatives Orozco and Rodriguez were listed as presenters.

Oakdale's Environmental Management Commission met October 19 at seven in the evening at the Oakdale Discovery Center on a forty million dollar bond referendum the county is proposing for the November 3 election.

Serena Raths and Emily Jorgensen of Washington County presented on the Land and Water Legacy Program. The program was created in November 2006 with a twenty million dollar voter-approved referendum for land and water protection. Over fifty-three million dollars has been invested, nineteen million from county funds and thirty-four million from partnership funds.

The proposed 2026 bonds would cost an estimated twenty-four dollars and sixty cents a year for twenty years on a median residential homestead valued at four hundred twenty thousand, nine hundred dollars. Agricultural homesteads would see three dollars per one hundred thousand of taxable value. Agricultural non-homesteads would see six dollars per one hundred thousand.

Washington County commissioners met Tuesday at nine in the morning in the County Board Room on a resolution to set a November 17 public hearing for up to forty million dollars in general obligation capital improvement bonds.

The five-year Capital Improvement Plan for 2027 through 2031 would finance the South Shop Improvements Project, Park Grove Library Improvements, and R.H. Stafford Library Improvements.

The board was also asked to accept a one million, thirty-one thousand dollar Byrne Discretionary Community Project Grant for the Sheriff's Office, covering June 1, 2026, through May 31, 2030, and to approve a one million, eight hundred sixty-six thousand, two hundred eighty-five dollar and seventy-eight cent purchase order with Axon Enterprise for the period November 1, 2026, through October 31, 2031.

Consent items included a two hundred fifty-four thousand, two dollar and twenty cent purchase order with Atmosphere Commercial Interiors for Law Enforcement Center furniture and a two hundred eighty-seven thousand, seven hundred forty-six dollar and sixty-two cent contract with Prevolv for Park Grove Library ancillary furniture.

A later workshop covered a proposed property exchange between the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources and the National Park Service for the Fairy Falls Day Use Area and the St. Croix Boom Site Wayside, plus the South Shop project.

Stillwater's council met Tuesday night for public hearings on proposed assessments for street and sidewalk projects and for delinquent fees.

It also considered a resolution for 2026 general obligation bonds, a feasibility study for the 2027 street improvement project, and a land exchange with the National Park Service.

The council met at seven in the evening at Stillwater City Hall, two hundred sixteen Fourth Street North. A workshop began at four-thirty in the afternoon.

Lake Elmo's Planning Commission meets Monday on a variance for a new eight hundred seventy-two square foot detached garage at eleven thousand fifty-five Thirty-second Street North.

Doug and Kelly Biever want to construct the garage, remove the existing five hundred seventy-nine square foot structure and other impervious surface, and relocate the driveway. The lot is zero point six acres zoned Rural Single Family with a Shoreland Overlay. City code sets a maximum impervious surface coverage of twenty-five percent. The property already exceeds that limit: thirty point nine percent now, after earlier renovations that left it at thirty-two point nine percent and thirty-three point eight percent before that.

Staff recommends approval with conditions that keep the finished coverage at twenty-eight point six percent, require the existing impervious to be removed first, and call for materials that match the house plus a vegetative buffer review with the Washington County Conservation District. The variance would expire if work does not start within twelve months.

The existing garage is too small and angled, forcing maneuvering onto neighboring property. Boat storage is common for lakeshore property but restricted in front yards.

The commission meets at six-thirty in the evening at thirty-eight eighty Laverne Avenue North.

Stillwater's Parks and Recreation Commission meets Monday night on a covered outdoor hockey rink for the Stillwater Area Hockey Association and approval of a new park sign design.

The agenda also includes a presentation on the Land and Water Legacy Referendum from Washington County and unfinished business on the Lumberjack Landing Guiding Document.

The commission meets at seven in the evening.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
